body:
While I out walking, the world desert...I happened upon a clump of datura growing in an otherwise wasted, barren, fallow corn field. Datura is a silly name for this plant. Now that weve been introduced, Im forced to call it the Witch Pepper, or prickled pepper.
I had read experiences of Witch pepper intoxication with fascination and wonder, but also frustration. Most reports I've read end in disaster, the people eat too much in environments that arent conducive to psychic experiments. So in the name of caution, in the spirit of science, I undertook a series of experiments to test the baseline dose of this mind-boggling plant. But be advised, these plants are highly variable. What I experience may not be typical.
Experiments conducted on three consecutive nights using one freshly-picked prickled pepper. Pepper was growing in poor soil; it was picked October 5th, Latitude: 41 degrees north, in a year when Autumn came a little early. The pepper was still green, and the seeds were wrinkled and juicy. The flowers were white and purple, still in bloom. The biggest plants were about waist-high.
Night One: 8 pepper seeds
I had just found the peppers on my walk home, and when I got home I was locked out. So I cut open my new find and started nibbling (I knew someone would come home eventually). I sat outside and started a fire. About 30 minutes, maybe an hour later I felt an odd feeling of warmth and contentment pass over me. And thats it: a tinge of sleepiness, but without the heavy eyelids. The feeling of drifting off without actually drifting off. It felt nice.
Night Two: 20 seeds
(I was frustrated with myself for more than doubling my dose. I had wanted to go about this step-wise) At this dose, the dry-mouth became noticeable. Outside, I think I heard phantom noises (they couldve been real, but after I realized they might be hallucinations, they died awaycoincidence, or phantom noises). I spoiled my experiment by smoking a little weed, but regardlessthis is definitely an active dose.
Night Three: 11 seeds
Back to familiar territory. No dry mouth. No hallucinations. Just warmth and relaxation. I notice this third night that the Witch Pepper is definitely addictive at these low doses. Also, its something of an aphrodisiac. It seems to excite the body and quiet the mind, so its not exactly good for sleep, but it is a useful tool for meditation!  I had the lurking sense, by the third day, that my body hadnt fully metabolized the previous days dose
. So I took a break. I didnt want toxins building up in my system. But ask me if I like this plant? You bet I do!
I personally love this plant, now.
I plan to work my way step-wise up to visual hallucinations, and get a rough sketch of the territory. But Ill need a good sitter before I go too much further. Know. Will. Dare. And Be Safe!
